Hi Alex — great to hear and thanks for the clear goals. We can run the hands-on and the load trial as part of the same engagement; typical plan we've seen work well is: 60–75 minute hands-on prompt review + routing configuration, then a 45–60 minute burst load run (can be the same or a follow-up day depending on how much prep you want on the dataset).

We are available for the Wed Aug 12, 14:00–15:30 PST slot — I'll tentatively hold that on everyone's calendars. Backup Thu Aug 13 morning also works.

Pre-kickoff checklist (attached):
- Prompt archive (examples + edge cases)
- Representative traffic profile (concurrency per-minute, average tokens per call)
- Any blocked endpoints / network restrictions
- A contact for sandbox creds and SSO details

Attachments: redwood-poc-template.xlsx, pre-kickoff-checklist.pdf

Draft agenda for Wed 12 (120 minutes):
- 14:00 Intro & success criteria (10m)
- 14:10 Prompt review + routing rules (45m)
- 14:55 Break / upload prep (10m)
- 15:05 Burst load trial (30m)
- 15:35 Observations, next steps (15m)

Success criteria (please confirm):
- Routing correctly directs at least 95% of high-priority prompts to the low-latency path
- Sustained concurrency target of 80 sessions/min with median per-token latency < 120ms
- No PII leakage observed in model outputs for provided test prompts

I'll create a meeting link and share a pre-POC doc with details and folders. Rishi / Marissa — tagging you for any prep items on capacity and SDK access.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Quick note from the capacity side: for the load trial we recommend reserving a short Dedicated bucket for the burst window if you expect sustained parallelism; otherwise we can run on hosted with a throttled profile. If your procurement team is OK with a short reserved burst it gives us tighter latency guarantees for the test.

Also, could you share a sanitized sample dataset so we can pre-warm KV cache behavior and validate tokenization differences before the session? That'll help reduce flakiness during the live burst.
